name: TinyAGI
vibe_summary: A multi-agent, multi-team orchestrator (formerly TinyClaw) aimed at running a 'one person company' of AI agents with isolated workspaces. Ships a polished web portal (TinyOffice), team chat rooms, and Linear-style task management on top of Claude Code and Codex CLIs.
best_for: Solo founders wanting a team of coordinated AI agents
Users who want a visual dashboard for agent teams
People already using Claude Code or Codex CLIs
avoid_if: You want strong sandboxing without extra infra (relies on gVisor)
You prefer a single lightweight assistant over multi-agent orchestration
openclaw_advantages: Native multi-team orchestration with agent hand-offs and fan-out
Built-in web portal with task/project management and live dashboards
One-command install with zero-config first run
Persistent team chat rooms and SQLite-backed task queue
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller community and ecosystem than OpenClaw
Experimental stability flag vs OpenClaw's maturity
Docker runs as root; sandboxing delegated to external gVisor
Fewer messaging channels (Discord/WhatsApp/Telegram vs OpenClaw's wider set)
confidence_summary: README and commit history give solid evidence of features and active development, but there are zero Reddit mentions and web sentiment is mostly about OpenClaw itself, so community and security assessments carry real uncertainty.

overview_markdown:
TinyAGI (formerly TinyClaw) is a TypeScript-based multi-agent orchestrator positioned as an 'agent teams' platform for the one-person company. It runs multiple isolated AI agents with specialized roles that collaborate via chain execution and fan-out, coordinated through a SQLite-backed queue with retry and dead-letter handling. Agents are powered by external CLIs — Claude Code for Anthropic and Codex CLI for OpenAI — plus any OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible custom endpoint, with per-provider API key management built in.

Its standout differentiator versus OpenClaw is the team-of-agents model paired with a rich control surface: TinyOffice, a browser portal with a pixel-office visualization, team chat rooms, a live TUI dashboard, and a recently added Linear-style task/project system with comments and sequential task IDs. Messaging channels include Discord, WhatsApp, and Telegram, and a plugin system supports message hooks and event listeners.

The project is explicitly experimental and moving fast — recent commits show heavy UI reorganization, a control plane with daemon restart and pairing APIs, and Docker hardening changes (including running as root in-container while delegating isolation to gVisor). Compared to OpenClaw's massive ecosystem and channel breadth, TinyAGI trades maturity and community for a more opinionated, team-oriented orchestration experience with a very low-friction install.
